newsitem.title: UK: Copper option vols climb higher, but volume modest.
newsitem.headline: Copper option vols climb higher, but volume modest.

text.p: LME copper volatility surged this week on the back of a heated underlying market, but volumes were only moderate and little fresh customer business was seen, traders said.
"Most of the action on copper options has come from market makers," one said.
Volatility traded this week as high as 23.0 to 23.5 percent on May, up from around 15.0 percent a week ago.
Implied at-the-money (ATM) volatility for May was quoted by some traders at 21.0/24.0 percent, but one said there had been some selling on Friday morning and vols were off a bit at 20.0/22.00.
"June has traded up to 20.5 percent, but there was some spec selling this morning and it was last at 18.5," he said.
June volatility was bid at 18.0-19.0 percent, July at 17.0-18.0 percent and fourth quarter at 15.0-16.0 percent.
The largest volume of the week was seen on Tuesday, when the move in the futures took off and 11,524 lots traded in copper.
"But that's really nothing for copper. It easily could have been 20,000 on a move like that," a trader said.

Market makers were overall long, saturated after a constant barrage of options sold late last year and early in 1997, traders said. Most of that selling was thought to have been from a large Korean player who sold straddles, with puts around $2,250 and calls at $2,450.
Light producer enquiry has been seen in copper, but not much business.
"At the highs, I would have expected some producer min-maxs or puts, but so far they're not doing much," a trader said.
Aluminium was less active, with vols marked up slightly with copper.

One trader saw some short-covering of May options at $1,575/$1,600 at 18.5 percent and buying of $1,600/$1,650 by those who were worried about the upside. Another said some downside puts have been purchased.

Vols were quoted for May at 16.0 to 19.0 percent, up three to four points on the week, but the others dates were only slightly firmer. June was at 15.0 to 18.0 percent and fourth quarter at 15.25 to 16.5 percent.
"A lot of people were hoping the vols would pick up so they could sell, but they haven't much," a trader said.
Business in the other metals was lacklustre.
In zinc, hedge funds bought some $1,300 calls for the first quarter 1998, bid at 19.0 percent, and financed by selling second quarter 1998 puts, a trader said.
Vols for May were quoted from 18.0 to 23.00 percent and June at 18.5 to 22.5 percent, up about one point.
Nickel was also slow, but a trader said on Friday morning some ATM selling had been seen in May to take advantage of time decay over the weekend.
Vols were quoted at 20.0 to 25.0 percent.
